_comment: The current targeting snapshot, loaded by `manage.py targeting_import --from-manifest`. Rebuilding this dataset from source costs 30-45 minutes of API calls and can exhaust WorldPop's daily quota for everyone else, so a new environment should restore from here rather than re-fetch. Pin a new drive_file_id whenever the dataset changes materially: export, upload to the folder below (shared with connect-labs-sa), and update the id, created_at and counts in one commit so the file and the record stay together.
notes: Restore with: make manage CMD="targeting_import --from-manifest" (needs LABS_SYNTHETIC_GDRIVE_SA_KEY; already in the ECS task definition, and locally readable from Secrets Manager as labs-jj-synthetic-gdrive-sa-key with the labs AWS profile). 102,903 values against 54,136 three days ago. Four raster sources joined the API ones: MAP's malaria surfaces (241.9M P. falciparum cases and 645,961 deaths for Africa, against the WHO World Malaria Report's ~246M and ~569k) which give malaria as COUNTS at every level; WorldPop's 1 km UN-adjusted grid, which finished the population backfill its own statistics API had refused, for the total AND the age bands (pop_u1/pop_u5/pop_f_15_49 now 778/778 at ADM1 and ~1,515/1,518 at ADM2, where pop_u1 had been 742); MAP's accessibility surface crossed with that grid (242.9M people beyond two hours' walk from care); and GHS-SMOD for DEGURBA rural share (745.2M rural Africans). The age bands are 2022 and the total is 2020 -- both UN-adjusted, so the two calibrations agree. cc-by-3.0 is MAP's and permits commercial use with attribution. Research notes are NOT in this snapshot -- they live in git and are written by `manage.py seed_targeting_research`, which should be run after any import.
